You can find documentaries by Louis Theroux. They're all really well done.

For sure, Adam Curtis' The Century of the Self.

  • Part one
  • Part two
  • Part three
  • Part four

As summarized by wikipedia:

The Century of the Self is a 2002 British television documentary series by Adam Curtis. It focuses on how the work of Sigmund Freud, Anna Freud, and Edward Bernays influenced the way corporations and governments have analyzed, dealt with, and controlled people.

Part one is a little slow as it lays a lot of background and groundwork for the subsequent episodes, but it's well worth it.

This is an amazing documentary and I agree with the post. It will blow your mind and make you see the world with a fresh pair of eyes. I would also recommend Curtis' other documentaries: Pandora's Box, The Power of Nightmares, and All Watched Over by Machines of Loving Grace.
Money for Nothing about the federal reserve is one of the best documentaries I've ever seen.

I've got a couple. One that I would highly recommend is NY77: The Coolest Year in Hell. It's about the year 1977 in NYC and showcases all the crazy shit that went on, causing it to one of the most pivotal moments in modern US history. I also wrote a review about it here in case you want more details.

Next up is Style Wars a documentary about Graffiti culture in early 80's New York. The documentarian for this is absolutely stunning, and there's a really memorable scene where he's interviewing a recently busted Graff artist who's in his Kitchen, and his mom is there talking shit about his choice of artistic expression as he's being interviewed. It's brilliant stuff.

Another brilliant one is The Corporation which is based on a book with the same name. The film takes a test for diagnosing psychopathy and applies it to a modern day corporation. There's some eye opening interviews with some really bright people, and it serves as a fantastic examination of how corporations operate and why.

The last one is actually a three part miniseries called The Wall Street Code which shows you how modern day Wall Street operates and how completely rigged the system is once you break it down. Fascinating and extremely educational documentary.
I watched Style Wars when it was on Netflix instant viewing (it's gone now). That was a really good doc. I'm going to check out the NY77 - sounds really interesting.

"The West" on PBS, the inspiring and tragic story of America's early expansion westward. I knew Native Americans were given a raw deal but god damn I had no idea just how sad the story of their decline really is.
Earth 2100 (link to playlist) is about the "worst case scenario" of earth this century. It was an ABC special, but nonetheless, it is a highly thought provoking piece.
